input_domain: Exact Python integer coefficients or exact decimal integer strings. int() coercion is not a validator for arbitrary floating inputs; the bound literal/census producers must preserve the integer domain.
mathematical_findings: For binary guard0, both original and capped rows hold because every RHS weight is nonnegative.
For guard1, a selected weight at least demand makes either row true; otherwise all selected weights are unchanged. Dividing by the positive gcd preserves the inequality.
Same-anchor coordinatewise cross-products imply the second nonnegative weighted sum is at least the demand-scaled first sum. Missing coordinates have zero weight.
An empty support becomes x_a <= 0. It dominates every same-anchor guard row; no nonempty support dominates it.
Dominance is transitive, so frontier replacements preserve coverage. The final pass verifies a direct authoritative or final-frontier witness for every raw candidate.
The helper does not alter authoritative rows or input origins; later model assembly must retain the full authoritative prefix.
review_scope: Proof helper; full census inputs, provenance and output receive their separate source/cold binding.
